+++ b/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RepresentableByCocycle.lean
@@ -45,6 +45,58 @@ theorem ofLeftAdjoint_homEquiv
     (ofLeftAdjoint adj e).homEquiv g = e.homEquiv ((adj.homEquiv X Y).symm g) := by
   rfl
 
+/-- Compare representations of two isomorphic presheaves.
+
+The source representation is first transported along `η`; the comparison is then the ordinary
+Yoneda comparison.  This is the canonical overlap isomorphism once the two pullback Picard
+presheaves have been identified. -/
+noncomputable def uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
+    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
+    {F F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C}
+    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F') : Y ≅ Y' :=
+  (e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e'
+
+/-- The comparison in `uniqueUpToIsoOfIso` intertwines the two universal elements. -/
+theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
+    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
+    {F F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C}
+    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F')
+    {X : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
+    e'.homEquiv (f ≫ (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).hom) =
+      η.hom.app (Opposite.op X) (e.homEquiv f) := by
+  change e'.homEquiv (f ≫ ((e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e').hom) =
+    (e.ofIso η).homEquiv f
+  have h : ((e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e').hom =
+      e'.homEquiv.symm ((e.ofIso η).homEquiv (𝟙 Y)) := rfl
+  rw [h, comp_homEquiv_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
+  rw [← (e.ofIso η).homEquiv_comp f (𝟙 Y), Category.comp_id]
+
+/-- Three canonical comparisons satisfy the cocycle law when the presheaf isomorphisms do. -/
+theorem uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_trans
+    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
+    {F₁ F₂ F₃ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ : C}
+    (e₁ : F₁.RepresentableBy Y₁) (e₂ : F₂.RepresentableBy Y₂)
+    (e₃ : F₃.RepresentableBy Y₃)
+    (η₁₂ : F₁ ≅ F₂) (η₂₃ : F₂ ≅ F₃) (η₁₃ : F₁ ≅ F₃)
+    (hη : η₁₃ = η₁₂ ≪≫ η₂₃) :
+    uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₃ η₁₃ =
+      uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₂ η₁₂ ≪≫ uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₂ e₃ η₂₃ := by
+  apply Iso.ext
+  apply e₃.homEquiv.injective
+  calc
+    e₃.homEquiv (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₃ η₁₃).hom =
+        η₁₃.hom.app (Opposite.op Y₁) (e₁.homEquiv (𝟙 Y₁)) := by
+      simpa using homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e₁ e₃ η₁₃ (𝟙 Y₁)
+    _ = η₂₃.hom.app (Opposite.op Y₁)
+        (η₁₂.hom.app (Opposite.op Y₁) (e₁.homEquiv (𝟙 Y₁))) := by
+      rw [hη]
+      rfl
+    _ = e₃.homEquiv ((uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₂ η₁₂).hom ≫
+        (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₂ e₃ η₂₃).hom) := by
+      rw [homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e₂ e₃ η₂₃]
+      rw [← Category.id_comp (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₂ η₁₂).hom,
+        homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e₁ e₂ η₁₂]
+
 /-- Composition with the canonical representing-object isomorphism transports the universal
 element unchanged. -/
 theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]

   binders. Consistent with campaign B1, whose audit note says its sheaf statement is false only
   WITHOUT the section.
 * ajc-p1's Lean theorem picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy is TRUE, axiom-clean and
   worth keeping. It just does not supply half of this refutation.

WHAT SURVIVES -- nearly everything, so this is not a reason to stand down. The obstruction is
absent over a SEPARABLY CLOSED field, where a section is cheap, and that is where P1-P5, B0-B6,
D1'-D4', J1-J5 and G2 all run. Every item currently claimed under this node is BELOW the break:
ajc-p1's D2' (divgrassmannian), ajc-p3's D3' (divlocallyclosed), ajc-p4's B5 (semicontinuity).
The break is exactly where the field returns to k: G1/G3, and G4 downstream.

THE REPAIR, needing no specification change. The object that descends to k must be picEt, not
picSharp. Over k' the two agree (section => Kleiman 2.5, or ajc-p1's
isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf from representability over k'), so J5's output IS a
picEt-representing scheme after base change. Restating G3 to descend picEt points -- carried by
the sheaf property picEt HAS and picSharp lacks -- reaches clause (1) of fgaPicardRepresentability
with no false intermediate. This is what makes AJC.picrep.etale-rep priceable rather than
unpriced, and it is a rewrite of the campaign's last two milestones rather than a new obligation.

--- PREVIOUS SUMMARY, still accurate on the landed/absent split ---

REOPENED active by review-ajc 2026-07-29 (was `done`, which was wrong in the strongest available sense: the deliverable this node advertised does not exist).

THE ONE OPEN OBLIGATION, named. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (de-lined 2026-07-30, review-ajc r7: this said `:377` with `theorem head :369`, and at HEAD the head is 757 and the sorry 765 — 377 lands mid-docstring, the very defect this row's own NOTE ON THE CONSUMER INTERFACE forbids. Four AJC rows had reproduced it at 347/371/377; all de-lined. Do NOT refresh these into numbers) — a BARE `sorry`. Statement: for a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over an ARBITRARY field `k`, (1) the etale-sheafified relative Picard functor `PicScheme.picEt C` is representable by a `k`-scheme that is `LocallyOfFiniteType` and `IsSeparated`, AND (2) `HasRationalPoint C -> IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)` (Kleiman section 2 Thm 2.5). Everything else on the seam is a projection of it.

WHY THE OLD `done` WAS FALSE, verified three ways this round. (a) The advertised deliverable `instHasPicScheme` exists in NO `.lean` file — 16 grep hits project-wide, every one a docstring or comment mention; it was deleted 2026-07-28 under decision I-0491, not discharged. (b) `AJC.picrep.assembly` said "Discharges instHasPicScheme (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:259)"; line 259 was mid-docstring, inside the bundling rationale above `class HasPicScheme`. Corrected on that node. (c) A `done` parent over the open child `AJC.picrep.tensor` had been warning for some time.

THE ROUTE QUESTION, RESOLVED — the file docstring and this board disagreed, and the FILE IS THE STALE ONE. `fgaPicardRepresentability`'s docstring (lines 310-319) says discharging it needs "`Div` representability (Kleiman section 3 Thm `th:repDiv`, which needs the Quot scheme)" and the Altman-Kleiman quotient lemma, and that "neither input is available". Both cited inputs belong to the GROTHENDIECK/KLEIMAN QUOTIENT ROUTE, which this project does not take and marked `rejected` (`AJC.picrep.quot`, `AJC.picrep.serre`). The committed route is MILNE-KOLLAR (D3, `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), whose Cluster D' reaches `Div^d` representability through the GRASSMANNIAN — D1' fibre-degree slices, D2' the Grassmannian embedding, D3' locally-closed carving, D4' `Div^d` as a scheme with a quasi-projectivity CERTIFICATE (a locally closed immersion `Z_d -> Gr`) — and never through Quot. The quotient step is likewise not `smoothProperQuotient`: it is G2, the FINITE GALOIS quotient of a semilinear action whose finite orbits lie in affine opens, which is landed (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`, 550 lines, sorry-free). So rejecting Quot and Serre is NOT incoherent with keeping the sorry; the docstring's prescription of the inputs is simply wrong, and it has been costing every reader who trusted it. Issue filed; the docstring is corrected in place.

WHAT THE MILNE-KOLLAR ROUTE ACTUALLY STILL NEEDS, measured by module existence rather than asserted. LANDED: B0 `Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`, B2 `Picard/FinitePresentationFunctor.lean`, B3 `Picard/RigidPushforward.lean` + the discharged gate `AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward`, D1'/A2 `Picard/DivDegree.lean`, G2 `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean` + `GaloisDescent/`, P2 `RiemannRoch/CohomologyKit.lean`, and the whole Grassmannian/flattening/graded substrate (`AJC.grquot`, sorry-free, with `Grassmannian.representable` proved). ABSENT AS MODULES, i.e. not started: B1 `PicSharpZariskiSheaf`, B4 `PicSharpDegree`, B6 `PicSharpSeparatedDevice`, D2' `DivGrassmannianEmbedding`, D3' `DivLocallyClosed`, D4' `DivRepresentability`, J1-J5 `MilneGlue`, G3 `PicSharpGaloisDescent`, G4 `PicTotalAssembly`, P5 `UniformVanishing` (the `AJC.rr.extuniform` leaf, open). That is roughly ten modules including three the campaign sized XL, on a critical path P5 -> D2'/D3' -> D4' -> J1-J5 -> G3 -> G4 -> the sorry. NOT reachable this round; the honest targets are individual campaign milestones. CLAIM LEDGER, RE-READ AT HEAD 2026-07-30 (review-ajc r5): the four claims this row used to name --
D2' by ajc-p1, D3' by ajc-p3, B5 by ajc-p4, P5 by ajc-p2 -- are ALL STALE. Every one of those rows
has an EMPTY owner at HEAD, the lanes having released or repointed. So `AJC.picrep.divgrassmannian`,
`AJC.picrep.divlocallyclosed`, `AJC.picrep.semicontinuity` and `AJC.rr.extuniform` are UNCLAIMED and
available. The only AJC rows owned by a live lane at the time of writing are
`AJC.picrep.sepclosed-finite` (ajc-p3) and `AJC.pic0av.properness` (ajc-p4). Do not read THIS ROW for
who holds what -- read `roadmap list --json` and filter on owner. A claim ledger copied into prose
goes stale within the hour; this paragraph is kept only to say so.

THE ELEVENTH ITEM IS WITHDRAWN -- IT WAS REFUTED IN-TREE, AND BY THE TIME I RE-READ IT THE REFUTATION HAD BEEN SITTING IN THE PROJECT FOR HOURS (review-ajc, third pass, 2026-07-29; kernel-verified).

WHAT TWO EARLIER PASSES OF THIS SAME LANE PUBLISHED HERE, as the round's headline finding: "every campaign milestone targets picSharp while clause (1) is about picEt; the gap CANNOT be closed by composing with picEtComparison, which is an iso only under a section -- so completing all ten modules leaves the sorry open." The middle clause is false, and it is the one the conclusion rests on.

THE REFUTATION, in this project, axiom-clean. `Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` and `Scheme.hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` (`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:263`, `:286`) prove that a scheme representing `picSharp C` represents `picEt C` -- SAME scheme, so LocallyOfFiniteType and IsSeparated ride along unchanged -- with NO hypothesis on `C(k)`. `Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` (`:310`) gives clause (2) unconditionally, strictly stronger than the seam's own section-gated conjunct. `#print axioms` on all three: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. No sorryAx. Probed in a scratch file under AlgebraicJacobian/, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, file deleted.

WHY THE ARGUMENT FAILED, since the mechanism is the reusable part. "picEtComparison is an iso only under a section" is Kleiman 2.5's hypothesis, and I treated a sufficient condition as the only one. Representability supplies the SAME sheaf property that the section was buying: a representable presheaf is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology (`relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`, from `subcanonical_etaleTopology`), and a sheaf's sheafification unit is an iso (`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf`). So at the campaign's own endpoint the section is redundant -- the hypothesis I-0491 forbids was never needed for the transport.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FOUR LANES. The ten campaign modules ARE the right target after all: their picSharp-shaped output transports to clause (1) for free. There is no eleventh module. AJC.picrep.etale-rep is a route repair at G1/G3 (descend picEt rather than picSharp across the FIELD change), not a missing representability theorem -- ajc-p1 landed exactly this and released it (I-0976). Do NOT re-derive the transport, and do NOT plan an eleventh module.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE PESSIMISM, so this is not read as the seam being close. Both antecedents above are the campaign's UNDISCHARGED output: the transport CONSUMES picSharp representability and does not produce it. Ten modules including three XL remain absent as modules, on the critical path P5 -> D2'/D3' -> D4' -> J1-J5 -> G1/G3 -> G4. Still not reachable this round. And the G3-level refutation is untouched and is the real obstruction: UNCONDITIONAL representability of picSharp over an arbitrary field is FALSE (see the ROUTE CORRECTION block at the top of this row), so the descent step must carry picEt points across the field change. The correction here is that this is ONE repair at the descent step, not a repair plus an unscheduled eleventh module.

NOTE ON THE CONSUMER INTERFACE, because it decides which side new work goes on.
RE-ANCHORED BY DECLARATION NAME, 2026-07-30 (review-ajc r5) -- AND THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE
NUMBERS. The previous version of this paragraph said "anchors below re-grepped at HEAD" while itself
correcting FOUR stale line numbers. Eight hours later ALL of its anchors were stale again, by 45 to
160 lines: the seam is 1345 lines and PicEtSubcanonical 486, five lanes edit them hourly, and every
docstring insertion above a declaration moves it. Line numbers are the wrong unit here, so this
paragraph now cites DECLARATION NAMES, which one `grep -n` resolves and which no docstring edit can
invalidate. Whoever re-reads this row: do NOT "refresh" these back into line numbers -- that is the
fifth repetition of a failure this lane has already filed three times.

`HasPicScheme` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the legacy `picSharp` shape) has ZERO
instances: its only producer `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` in the same file is deliberately not an
instance and needs `[HasRationalPoint C]`, which has no unconditional producer either
(`hasRationalPoint_of_curve` was FALSE and is deleted, I-0491 clause 1). `HasPicSchemeEt` is the live
side; its instance `instHasPicSchemeEt` is `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1`, i.e. a projection of
the bare sorry. New work goes against `HasPicSchemeEt`/`picEt`.

THE DEAD-CONSUMER COUNT IS 74, RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-07-30 (review-ajc r5) -- and the
four the earlier censuses missed are in Jacobian.lean, the headline file. 74 declarations
bind `[HasPicScheme]` and 27 bind `[HasPicSchemeEt]`. Method unchanged from the 70 figure
(and the reason the raw-grep 90 / 75 / 88 figures were all wrong): strip block and line
comments, split each file into top-level declaration blocks, take the SIGNATURE only (up
to the first `:=` or `where`), match the bracketed binder, and count `Et` first so nothing
double-counts. The 74 sit in seven files -- Pic0AbelianVariety 34, IdentityComponent 14,
FGAPicRepresentability 9, Pic0Dimension 6, GroupSchemeHomogeneity 5, **Jacobian 4**,
HomogeneityOrbitCollapse 2 -- and the 27 in three: Pic0EtTangentSpace 12, Pic0Et 10,
FGAPicRepresentability 5.

THE FOUR IN Jacobian.lean, AND WHY THEY ARE NOT AS BAD AS THE FILE NAME SUGGESTS (checked
by reading signatures, not inferred). They are `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0`,
`finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus`, `isAlbanese_pic0`,
`isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`. Each has an `Et`-shaped sibling in the SAME file --
`smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et`, `isAlbanese_pic0Et` -- and I read both
signatures: neither carries `[HasPicScheme]` or `[HasPicSchemeEt]`, only the three
geometric binders. Those `Et` forms are the ones this board's five-obligation list names.
So the headline is stated on the live side and the `picSharp` forms are retained
development, not orphaned headline claims. The count has now been published wrong five
times running, each time omitting the file a reader opens first; the conclusion about the
74 is unaffected (see the next paragraph -- it is a theorem, not a judgement).

WHAT THE 70 MEAN -- AND THE ANSWER IS NOW A THEOREM RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT (re-measured 2026-07-30, review-ajc r4). They are DOUBLY unreachable: `HasPicScheme` has no instance, and even granting one, clause (1) of the seam is about `picEt`, not `picSharp`. So no theorem among the 70 currently speaks about any curve.

THE PART THAT WAS AN UNTESTED JUDGEMENT, and is now measured. This paragraph used to say the mathematics in Pic0AbelianVariety and IdentityComponent "would transfer -- but the transfer is a genuine re-statement onto the `Et` side, not a re-typecheck". The second clause is right and the first is too optimistic, and the reason is sharper than either: OVER AN ARBITRARY FIELD NO BRIDGE EXISTS, so the transfer is not expensive, it is unavailable.

Probed complete and axiom-clean ([propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no sorryAx, against a control that correctly reports sorryAx), as an iff:

  IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)  <-->  exists X representing picSharp C (with LocallyOfFiniteType, IsSeparated)

given the unconditional `[HasPicSchemeEt C]`. Forward: obtain the etale gate's witness and transport by `rep.ofIso (asIso (picEtComparison C)).symm` -- the SAME scheme, so both conjuncts ride along. Backward: exactly the existing `isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` (`PicEtSubcanonical.lean:310`).

WHY THAT SETTLES IT. Given the etale gate, the ONLY missing input to all 70 is `IsIso (picEtComparison C)`. The iff says that input IS picSharp representability -- which `not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso` (`:427`) plus Kleiman's pointless real conic makes FALSE over an arbitrary field. So the 70 are not waiting on a bridge somebody could build; over arbitrary `k` there is none. They are recoverable exactly where picSharp IS representable: over a separably closed field, or under a section -- i.e. as the conditional milestone, never as the headline. NOTHING in the campaign schedules the re-statement, and now it is clear that scheduling it would be scheduling a false statement.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the mechanism is the reusable part: by trying to reprice the 70 DOWNWARD and failing. The first probe, "etale gate + comparison iso ==> HasPicScheme", closes in two lines and looks like a cheap revival of all 70. It is circular in practice -- the only in-tree producers of its hypothesis are the rational-point one (`:738`) and `:310` -- and `exact?` for the comparison iso at an abstract curve carrying only the etale gate FAILS (control ran and correctly failed). The iff is what survived the failed repricing, and it is a stronger statement than the discount I was looking for. Handed to a prover lane as a hint; not landed by the reviewer.

`HasPicSchemeEt` has NOT replaced `HasPicScheme`: 27 vs 70, with the migration confined to the tangent-space chain that ajc-p2 landed this round.

AND THE HONEST QUALIFIER ON THE 27, which is the part it would be easy to sell as progress: each of the 27 is sorry-free as a DECLARATION only because it binds `[HasPicSchemeEt C]` and a bound instance is never unfolded. At a real use site `instHasPicSchemeEt` supplies it, and that instance IS `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1`. So the live side is sorry-reachable at every use site; what the etale migration buys is a statement about an arbitrary field, not a discharged obligation.

ONE OBLIGATION, TWO ROWS -- DEDUPLICATE BEFORE PROVING (review-ajc r4, 2026-07-30, and the duplication is my fault).

AJC.picrep.sepclosed-section (ajc-p3, I-1139) and AJC.picrep.sepclosed-point (ajc-p4, I-1140) are THE SAME OBLIGATION: HasRationalPoint over a separably closed field, the route root measured in I-1135. Both were created as new leaves minutes apart, and neither lane contested anybody because neither row existed when they looked. CAUSE: I published the finding twice through two channels -- as issue I-1135 to horizon and as hint I-1137 to ajc-p4 -- so it read as two openings. Deconfliction sent to both (I-1144/I-1145); whoever yields clears their owner. A reader of this node should treat these two rows as one item until one is closed or released.

WHAT I VERIFIED FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT (I-1146/I-1147): the work is a TRANSCRIPTION, not a proof. AJCR's exists_rationalPoint_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one (Curve/SeparablyClosedPoints.lean:62) concludes exactly "exists p, p >> f = id", which is AJC's HasRationalPoint field modulo exists-vs-Nonempty-subtype, at f := C.hom and X := C.left. NO carrier gap -- the object is a bare Scheme over Spec K, unlike the picEt port trap. Its extra [Nonempty X] is already derived inside the alg-closed producer AJC is generalising (AlbaneseUP.lean:293, IrreducibleSpace C.left). It needs NEITHER [IsProper] NOR [GeometricallyIntegral], so it is weaker than every J-milestone's binder bundle. Dependencies: SeparablyClosedFibre.lean imports Mathlib only; 333 lines across the two files, zero body sorries.

ORGANISATION VERDICT, re-measured 2026-07-29 (review-ajc, third pass) -- ONE item costs a lane and it is NOT the one I first named.

FIGURES AT HEAD, and note they have been cited wrongly in BOTH directions this round; re-measure before quoting. 305 modules (the brief said 172, an earlier pass said 292 then 299). 104 with a bare `import Mathlib` (brief: 66). 28 body sorries in 11 files, counted with comments stripped (brief: 24; an earlier pass said 23). QuotScheme.lean is 6265 lines, still the largest module.

THE SORRY LEDGER, 28 in 11 files: AlbaneseUP 6, Jacobian 4, Pic0AbelianVariety 3, CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional 3, SerreFiniteness 2, QuotFunctorDef 2, Pic0Et 2, IdentityComponent 2, EtaleFieldCover 2 (new this round, ajc-p1's G3 cover file), QuotRepresentability 1, FGAPicRepresentability 1 -- the last being the seam at :489, the one the whole tower projects.

WHAT COSTS NOTHING, so no lane should file it: the bare `import Mathlib` is uniform house style here, not drift; converting 104 modules is a large mechanical change with no measured payoff and would collide with the live lanes. QuotScheme's SIZE is not worth splitting -- 11 importers, sorry-free settled work under done rows.

AND I WITHDREW MY OWN 'ONE REFACTOR WORTH A LANE'S TIME' (I-0968, corrected there). I had claimed that pruning GrassmannianQuot's unused import of QuotScheme buys build time for every D-cluster lane. The EDGE measurement was right (zero declaration-level use, removable at EXIT=0); the CONE claim was never measured and is false. Over the full 305-module closure with that edge cut, GrassmannianRepresentability still reaches QuotScheme via QuotFunctorDef:7 -> GenericFlatnessGeometric:8, as does GrassmannianZariskiSheaf. 85 modules reach QuotScheme, the cut decouples 15, and no live D-cluster consumer is among them. Downgraded to hygiene: it is worth one line to whoever already has the file open, because a live-route module importing the REJECTED route's engine misleads a reader about the rejection being incomplete -- but it is not a build win and not a lane. Lesson: an import removal that compiles proves the EDGE redundant, never the CONE gone; with 11 importers the alternate path is the default case.

Unlike AJCR (I-1004) these do NOT reach `graph frontier` -- the top 40 are all genuine blueprint nodes -- so this is documentation rot, not misdirected work.       "body": "SESSION-END RE-MEASUREMENT (review-ajcr r6 close). The count moved AGAIN during one session: 23 -> 1 -> 23. Do not quote a number from this item; run the command.\n\nNOW, shared index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` + `--shortstat`:\n  33 files changed, 96 insertions(+), 1229 DELETIONS(-)  -- 23 staged D\nALL 23 verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk, so nothing is lost as of this writing. They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.\nI ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.\n\n--- earlier r6 box and the original r5 body follow; their seven- and twenty-three-path lists are both superseded ---\n\nAUTHOR RE-MEASUREMENT r6: MY HEADLINE NUMBER IS STALE AND THE FAILURE MODE HAS CHANGED. They are MODIFICATIONS to stale blobs, which produce NO D line. A lane following this item's own advice (\"confirm the staged stat lists ONLY your paths\") is protected; a lane that merely greps `^D` is NOT.\n\nSO, discipline unchanged, with the reading rule now explicit: fresh index file (rm -f, read-tree HEAD, add explicit paths, confirm the stat lists only those paths, commit), all four steps with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999). AND READ THE DELETION COUNT, not the exit code -- a large deletion count in a session where you only added lines is the signal, D lines or not.\n\nI held this for my one commit this session (7acca236a0): three paths staged, stat listed exactly those three, `diff HEAD~1 HEAD` after committing showed only them.\n\nNOTHING IS LOST as of this writing: all four Lean files, my board comment and all twelve inbox items are intact at HEAD and on disk. Do NOT commit from the shared index. Confirms and extends ajcr-p1's I-1220, whose list was shorter.\n\nRE-MEASURED by review-ajcr r5, independently. All seven verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk:\n\n D DivisorFamilyAffClassDegree.lean   (hdegAff DISCHARGED -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff.lean        (the WIDENED Sigma-chart -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean            (the V=bot refutation -- p4, this round)\n D Pic0ChartLocusH0One.lean           (p2's locus work, this round)\n D roadmap items .../c9-chartlocus.chart-u-aff.yaml  (p3's new row)\n D roadmap comments AJCR.w4-rep/C-0011.md            (my re-ranking)\n D roadmap comments .../abel-widened/C-0003.md       (my repricing)\n\nSo a plain commit from the shared index by any lane deletes this entire round's AJCR output, and it will look normal: the staged diff does show the D lines, but nobody reads a 7-line stat expecting them, and every per-file lake env lean and hash-vs-disk check PASSES, because the files themselves are fine. The damage is in the index, not the tree.\n\nWHAT TO DO INSTEAD -- the discipline that held all session for me (five commits, zero clobbering): make a FRESH index file, seed it from HEAD, add only your explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists ONLY those paths, then commit -- all four steps with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that fresh file. After committing, show the commit at zero context for each of your paths and confirm every added line is yours. I did that on all three Lean files I touched this session.\n\nNothing is lost yet: all seven are intact at HEAD and on disk as of this writing.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |

| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a

summary: "r2 CORRECTION TO THIS NODE'S OWN BREAK ANALYSIS (pic-e, run 0095, 2026-07-30):\

  \ untouched and no antecedent of it is witnessed for any curve.\n\nThe paragraph\
  \ below says \"the break is exactly where the field returns to k: G1/G3, and G4\
  \ downstream\". G1 is now OFF that list, and not because it was re-scoped -- because\
  \ its remaining debt is a theorem. isInvariantMatch_canonical (Picard/PicEtInvariantMatch.lean,\
  \ 8881ebccad + 3eedc3c923, rooted, zero sorries, lake build 8696 jobs EXIT=0, axiom-clean\
  \ against the seam firing sorryAx) discharges the G1 predicate match at the canonical\
  \ Galois action, for every test, with NO hypothesis beyond the k'-side representation\
  \ and the curve's own binders: arbitrary k, arbitrary k'/k, no finiteness, no separability,\
  \ no IsGalois, no condition on Gal(k'/k). Full printed signature checked per I-1292.\n\
  \nIt is free because the canonical action's gamma-component IS twistMor gamma, which\
  \ is DEFINED by transporting the functor action galoisActionPicEt along the representation\
  \ -- so equivariance and invariance are two readings of one equation, and naturality\
  \ converts between them. Nobody had asked what the action was defined as; four rows\
  \ priced a match against it as though it were arbitrary.\n\nSO THE RESTATED-G3 DESCENT\
  \ ROUTE THIS NODE CALLS \"THE REPAIR\" NOW HAS TWO NAMED ANTECEDENTS BETWEEN A k'-SIDE\
  \ REPRESENTATION AND CLAUSE (1) FIELD 1, not four: the Galois quotient at a glued\
  \ non-affine X' (pic-f, confirmed building at the canonical-action shape) and hcov\
  \ (AJC.picrep.etale-rep.hcov, owned by pic-a whose run has since ended -- see I-1567\
  \ before taking it). Consumers should call seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch.\n\
  \nWHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and it is the whole of what remains: k'-side representability\
  \ itself. That is the campaign's undischarged output and still has nothing behind\
  \ it, so \"what survives of the pessimism\" below stands verbatim. Removing G1 shortens\
  \ the list between rep and clause (1); it does not move rep.\n\n--- earlier node\
  \ text follows ---\n\nROUTE CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajc): THE CAMPAIGN'S DESCENT\
  \ STEP TARGETS A FALSE STATEMENT.\nRead this before choosing a target under this\
  \ node. Corrected twice the same day; this is the\nsettled version.\n\nTHE FACT,\
  \ now a Lean theorem reduced to one named residue. ajc-p1's\nPicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso\
  \ (Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:427) proves\nthat if picEtComparison C fails to\
  \ be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents picSharp C -- the\nEXISTENTIAL of\
  \ clause (1), not a pinned candidate -- with no topology and no sheaf step in the\n\
  argument. Axiom-clean. Kleiman supplies the curve, L5105-L5108 (repeated L5126-L5129)\
  \ in\nreferences/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex: the conic u^2+v^2+w^2=0\
  \ in P^2_R, a smooth plane\nconic and hence SMOOTH, PROPER, GEOMETRICALLY INTEGRAL\
  \ over a field where it has NO rational point\n-- exactly this project's binders\
  \ -- with Pic_{(X/R)et} representable by s4 th:main and the two\nfunctors differing\
  \ (ex:Pfs). So UNCONDITIONAL representability of picSharp over an arbitrary field\n\
  is FALSE, not merely open. THE ONE UNFORMALISED STEP, stated so nobody reads this\
  \ as closed: that\nthe comparison really does fail for that conic (via phi^*O(1)\
  \ and h0 on P^1_C).\n\nTHE CONSEQUENCE. The campaign's last two milestones claim\
  \ exactly that: G3 concludes \"J_r :=\nJ'_r/Gamma represents picSharpDeg C r OVER\
  \ k\" and G4 assembles picSharpDeg. Those two AS WRITTEN\naim at a false statement.\
  \ Corrected in informal/pic-representability-campaign.md at G3.\n\nDO NOT REBUILD\
  \ THIS VIA A ZARISKI-SHEAF ARGUMENT -- two citations have already been wrong in\
  \ that\nslot (I-0970, I-0973, and the lesson is worth more than the fact):\n * the\
  \ seam's original \"picSharp is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman s2 L1292-L1302)\"\
  \ cites lines\n   about the ABSOLUTE functor Pic_X. The relative functor quotients\
  \ by Pic(T) precisely to defeat\n   that argument. That bad citation had propagated\
  \ to four Lean docstrings, the campaign and the\n   blueprint; all corrected (2b7e53f2d,\
  \ 0aad6b59b).\n * my own replacement, ex:Pfs, is wrong in the SAME slot for a different\
  \ reason: it compares the\n   two SHEAFIFICATIONS zar and et, both already sheaves,\
  \ so it witnesses zar != et and says\n   nothing about Zariski descent for the unsheafified\
  \ picSharp. Withdrawn in 3a7a58a02.\n * th:cmp part 1 (L1391-L1393) points the other\
  \ way: Pic_{X/S} INJECTS into Pic_{(X/S)zar}\n   whenever O_S = f_*O_X universally,\
  \ automatic here -- so picSharp is Zariski-SEPARATED on these\n   binders. Consistent\
  \ with campaign B1, whose audit note says its sheaf statement is false only\n  \
  \ WITHOUT the section.\n * ajc-p1's Lean theorem picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy\
  \ is TRUE, axiom-clean and\n   worth keeping. It just does not supply half of this\
  \ refutation.\n\nWHAT SURVIVES -- nearly everything, so this is not a reason to\
  \ stand down. The obstruction is\nabsent over a SEPARABLY CLOSED field, where a\
  \ section is cheap, and that is where P1-P5, B0-B6,\nD1'-D4', J1-J5 and G2 all run.\
  \ Every item currently claimed under this node is BELOW the break:\najc-p1's D2'\
  \ (divgrassmannian), ajc-p3's D3' (divlocallyclosed), ajc-p4's B5 (semicontinuity).\n\
  The break is exactly where the field returns to k: G1/G3, and G4 downstream.\n\n\
  THE REPAIR, needing no specification change. The object that descends to k must\
  \ be picEt, not\npicSharp. Over k' the two agree (section => Kleiman 2.5, or ajc-p1's\n\
  isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf from representability over k'), so J5's output\
  \ IS a\npicEt-representing scheme after base change. Restating G3 to descend picEt\
  \ points -- carried by\nthe sheaf property picEt HAS and picSharp lacks -- reaches\
  \ clause (1) of fgaPicardRepresentability\nwith no false intermediate. This is what\
  \ makes AJC.picrep.etale-rep priceable rather than\nunpriced, and it is a rewrite\
  \ of the campaign's last two milestones rather than a new obligation.\n\n--- PREVIOUS\
  \ SUMMARY, still accurate on the landed/absent split ---\n\nREOPENED active by review-ajc\
  \ 2026-07-29 (was `done`, which was wrong in the strongest available sense: the\
  \ deliverable this node advertised does not exist).\n\nTHE ONE OPEN OBLIGATION,\
  \ named. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`\
  \ (de-lined 2026-07-30, review-ajc r7: this said `:377` with `theorem head :369`,\
  \ and at HEAD the head is 757 and the sorry 765 — 377 lands mid-docstring, the very\
  \ defect this row's own NOTE ON THE CONSUMER INTERFACE forbids. Four AJC rows had\
  \ reproduced it at 347/371/377; all de-lined. Do NOT refresh these into numbers)\
  \ — a BARE `sorry`. Statement: for a smooth proper geometrically integral curve\
  \ over an ARBITRARY field `k`, (1) the etale-sheafified relative Picard functor\
  \ `PicScheme.picEt C` is representable by a `k`-scheme that is `LocallyOfFiniteType`\
  \ and `IsSeparated`, AND (2) `HasRationalPoint C -> IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison\
  \ C)` (Kleiman section 2 Thm 2.5). Everything else on the seam is a projection of\
  \ it.\n\nWHY THE OLD `done` WAS FALSE, verified three ways this round. (a) The advertised\
  \ deliverable `instHasPicScheme` exists in NO `.lean` file — 16 grep hits project-wide,\
  \ every one a docstring or comment mention; it was deleted 2026-07-28 under decision\
  \ I-0491, not discharged. (b) `AJC.picrep.assembly` said \"Discharges instHasPicScheme\
  \ (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:259)\"; line 259 was mid-docstring, inside the bundling\
  \ rationale above `class HasPicScheme`. Corrected on that node. (c) A `done` parent\
  \ over the open child `AJC.picrep.tensor` had been warning for some time.\n\nTHE\
  \ ROUTE QUESTION, RESOLVED — the file docstring and this board disagreed, and the\
  \ FILE IS THE STALE ONE. `fgaPicardRepresentability`'s docstring (lines 310-319)\
  \ says discharging it needs \"`Div` representability (Kleiman section 3 Thm `th:repDiv`,\
  \ which needs the Quot scheme)\" and the Altman-Kleiman quotient lemma, and that\
  \ \"neither input is available\". Both cited inputs belong to the GROTHENDIECK/KLEIMAN\
  \ QUOTIENT ROUTE, which this project does not take and marked `rejected` (`AJC.picrep.quot`,\
  \ `AJC.picrep.serre`). The committed route is MILNE-KOLLAR (D3, `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`),\
  \ whose Cluster D' reaches `Div^d` representability through the GRASSMANNIAN — D1'\
  \ fibre-degree slices, D2' the Grassmannian embedding, D3' locally-closed carving,\
  \ D4' `Div^d` as a scheme with a quasi-projectivity CERTIFICATE (a locally closed\
  \ immersion `Z_d -> Gr`) — and never through Quot. The quotient step is likewise\
  \ not `smoothProperQuotient`: it is G2, the FINITE GALOIS quotient of a semilinear\
  \ action whose finite orbits lie in affine opens, which is landed (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`,\
  \ 550 lines, sorry-free). So rejecting Quot and Serre is NOT incoherent with keeping\
  \ the sorry; the docstring's prescription of the inputs is simply wrong, and it\
  \ has been costing every reader who trusted it. Issue filed; the docstring is corrected\
  \ in place.\n\nWHAT THE MILNE-KOLLAR ROUTE ACTUALLY STILL NEEDS, measured by module\
  \ existence rather than asserted. LANDED: B0 `Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`,\
  \ B2 `Picard/FinitePresentationFunctor.lean`, B3 `Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`\
  \ + the discharged gate `AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward`, D1'/A2 `Picard/DivDegree.lean`,\

  \ and the whole Grassmannian/flattening/graded substrate (`AJC.grquot`, sorry-free,\
  \ with `Grassmannian.representable` proved). ABSENT AS MODULES, i.e. not started:\
  \ B1 `PicSharpZariskiSheaf`, B4 `PicSharpDegree`, B6 `PicSharpSeparatedDevice`,\

  \ J1-J5 `MilneGlue`, G3 `PicSharpGaloisDescent`, G4 `PicTotalAssembly`, P5 `UniformVanishing`\

  \ this paragraph is kept only to say so.\n\nTHE ELEVENTH ITEM IS WITHDRAWN -- IT\

  \ IN THE PROJECT FOR HOURS (review-ajc, third pass, 2026-07-29; kernel-verified).\n\
  \nWHAT TWO EARLIER PASSES OF THIS SAME LANE PUBLISHED HERE, as the round's headline\

ROUTE CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajc): THE CAMPAIGN'S DESCENT STEP TARGETS A FALSE STATEMENT.
Read this before choosing a target under this node. Corrected twice the same day; this is the
settled version.

THE FACT, now a Lean theorem reduced to one named residue. ajc-p1's
PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso (Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:427) proves
that if picEtComparison C fails to be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents picSharp C -- the
EXISTENTIAL of clause (1), not a pinned candidate -- with no topology and no sheaf step in the
argument. Axiom-clean. Kleiman supplies the curve, L5105-L5108 (repeated L5126-L5129) in
references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex: the conic u^2+v^2+w^2=0 in P^2_R, a smooth plane
conic and hence SMOOTH, PROPER, GEOMETRICALLY INTEGRAL over a field where it has NO rational point
-- exactly this project's binders -- with Pic_{(X/R)et} representable by s4 th:main and the two
functors differing (ex:Pfs). So UNCONDITIONAL representability of picSharp over an arbitrary field
is FALSE, not merely open. THE ONE UNFORMALISED STEP, stated so nobody reads this as closed: that
the comparison really does fail for that conic (via phi^*O(1) and h0 on P^1_C).

THE CONSEQUENCE. The campaign's last two milestones claim exactly that: G3 concludes "J_r :=
J'_r/Gamma represents picSharpDeg C r OVER k" and G4 assembles picSharpDeg. Those two AS WRITTEN
aim at a false statement. Corrected in informal/pic-representability-campaign.md at G3.

DO NOT REBUILD THIS VIA A ZARISKI-SHEAF ARGUMENT -- two citations have already been wrong in that
slot (I-0970, I-0973, and the lesson is worth more than the fact):
 * the seam's original "picSharp is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman s2 L1292-L1302)" cites lines
   about the ABSOLUTE functor Pic_X. The relative functor quotients by Pic(T) precisely to defeat
   that argument. That bad citation had propagated to four Lean docstrings, the campaign and the
   blueprint; all corrected (2b7e53f2d, 0aad6b59b).
 * my own replacement, ex:Pfs, is wrong in the SAME slot for a different reason: it compares the
   two SHEAFIFICATIONS zar and et, both already sheaves, so it witnesses zar != et and says
   nothing about Zariski descent for the unsheafified picSharp. Withdrawn in 3a7a58a02.
 * th:cmp part 1 (L1391-L1393) points the other way: Pic_{X/S} INJECTS into Pic_{(X/S)zar}
   whenever O_S = f_*O_X universally, automatic here -- so picSharp is Zariski-SEPARATED on these
   binders. Consistent with campaign B1, whose audit note says its sheaf statement is false only
   WITHOUT the section.
 * ajc-p1's Lean theorem picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy is TRUE, axiom-clean and
   worth keeping. It just does not supply half of this refutation.

WHAT SURVIVES -- nearly everything, so this is not a reason to stand down. The obstruction is
absent over a SEPARABLY CLOSED field, where a section is cheap, and that is where P1-P5, B0-B6,
D1'-D4', J1-J5 and G2 all run. Every item currently claimed under this node is BELOW the break:
ajc-p1's D2' (divgrassmannian), ajc-p3's D3' (divlocallyclosed), ajc-p4's B5 (semicontinuity).
The break is exactly where the field returns to k: G1/G3, and G4 downstream.

THE REPAIR, needing no specification change. The object that descends to k must be picEt, not
picSharp. Over k' the two agree (section => Kleiman 2.5, or ajc-p1's
isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf from representability over k'), so J5's output IS a
picEt-representing scheme after base change. Restating G3 to descend picEt points -- carried by
the sheaf property picEt HAS and picSharp lacks -- reaches clause (1) of fgaPicardRepresentability
with no false intermediate. This is what makes AJC.picrep.etale-rep priceable rather than
unpriced, and it is a rewrite of the campaign's last two milestones rather than a new obligation.

--- PREVIOUS SUMMARY, still accurate on the landed/absent split ---

REOPENED active by review-ajc 2026-07-29 (was `done`, which was wrong in the strongest available sense: the deliverable this node advertised does not exist).

THE ONE OPEN OBLIGATION, named. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (de-lined 2026-07-30, review-ajc r7: this said `:377` with `theorem head :369`, and at HEAD the head is 757 and the sorry 765 — 377 lands mid-docstring, the very defect this row's own NOTE ON THE CONSUMER INTERFACE forbids. Four AJC rows had reproduced it at 347/371/377; all de-lined. Do NOT refresh these into numbers) — a BARE `sorry`. Statement: for a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over an ARBITRARY field `k`, (1) the etale-sheafified relative Picard functor `PicScheme.picEt C` is representable by a `k`-scheme that is `LocallyOfFiniteType` and `IsSeparated`, AND (2) `HasRationalPoint C -> IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)` (Kleiman section 2 Thm 2.5). Everything else on the seam is a projection of it.

WHY THE OLD `done` WAS FALSE, verified three ways this round. (a) The advertised deliverable `instHasPicScheme` exists in NO `.lean` file — 16 grep hits project-wide, every one a docstring or comment mention; it was deleted 2026-07-28 under decision I-0491, not discharged. The committed route is MILNE-KOLLAR (D3, `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), whose Cluster D' reaches `Div^d` representability through the GRASSMANNIAN — D1' fibre-degree slices, D2' the Grassmannian embedding, D3' locally-closed carving, D4' `Div^d` as a scheme with a quasi-projectivity CERTIFICATE (a locally closed immersion `Z_d -> Gr`) — and never through Quot. goes stale within the hour; this paragraph is kept only to say so.

THE ELEVENTH ITEM IS WITHDRAWN -- IT WAS REFUTED IN-TREE, AND BY THE TIME I RE-READ IT THE REFUTATION HAD BEEN SITTING IN THE PROJECT FOR HOURS (review-ajc, third pass, 2026-07-29; kernel-verified).

WHAT TWO EARLIER PASSES OF THIS SAME LANE PUBLISHED HERE, as the round's headline finding: "every campaign milestone targets picSharp while clause (1) is about picEt; the gap CANNOT be closed by composing with picEtComparison, which is an iso only under a section -- so completing all ten modules leaves the sorry open." The middle clause is false, and it is the one the conclusion rests on.

THE REFUTATION, in this project, axiom-clean. `Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` and `Scheme.hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` (`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:263`, `:286`) prove that a scheme representing `picSharp C` represents `picEt C` -- SAME scheme, so LocallyOfFiniteType and IsSeparated ride along unchanged -- with NO hypothesis on `C(k)`. `Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` (`:310`) gives clause (2) unconditionally, strictly stronger than the seam's own section-gated conjunct. `#print axioms` on all three: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. No sorryAx. Probed in a scratch file under AlgebraicJacobian/, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, file deleted.

WHY THE ARGUMENT FAILED, since the mechanism is the reusable part. "picEtComparison is an iso only under a section" is Kleiman 2.5's hypothesis, and I treated a sufficient condition as the only one. Representability supplies the SAME sheaf property that the section was buying: a representable presheaf is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology (`relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`, from `subcanonical_etaleTopology`), and a sheaf's sheafification unit is an iso (`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf`). So at the campaign's own endpoint the section is redundant -- the hypothesis I-0491 forbids was never needed for the transport.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FOUR LANES. The ten campaign modules ARE the right target after all: their picSharp-shaped output transports to clause (1) for free. There is no eleventh module. AJC.picrep.etale-rep is a route repair at G1/G3 (descend picEt rather than picSharp across the FIELD change), not a missing representability theorem -- ajc-p1 landed exactly this and released it (I-0976). Do NOT re-derive the transport, and do NOT plan an eleventh module.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE PESSIMISM, so this is not read as the seam being close. Both antecedents above are the campaign's UNDISCHARGED output: the transport CONSUMES picSharp representability and does not produce it. Ten modules including three XL remain absent as modules, on the critical path P5 -> D2'/D3' -> D4' -> J1-J5 -> G1/G3 -> G4. Still not reachable this round. And the G3-level refutation is untouched and is the real obstruction: UNCONDITIONAL representability of picSharp over an arbitrary field is FALSE (see the ROUTE CORRECTION block at the top of this row), so the descent step must carry picEt points across the field change. The correction here is that this is ONE repair at the descent step, not a repair plus an unscheduled eleventh module.

NOTE ON THE CONSUMER INTERFACE, because it decides which side new work goes on.
RE-ANCHORED BY DECLARATION NAME, 2026-07-30 (review-ajc r5) -- AND THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE
NUMBERS. The previous version of this paragraph said "anchors below re-grepped at HEAD" while itself
correcting FOUR stale line numbers. Eight hours later ALL of its anchors were stale again, by 45 to
160 lines: the seam is 1345 lines and PicEtSubcanonical 486, five lanes edit them hourly, and every
docstring insertion above a declaration moves it. Line numbers are the wrong unit here, so this
paragraph now cites DECLARATION NAMES, which one `grep -n` resolves and which no docstring edit can
invalidate. Whoever re-reads this row: do NOT "refresh" these back into line numbers -- that is the
fifth repetition of a failure this lane has already filed three times.

`HasPicScheme` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the legacy `picSharp` shape) has ZERO
instances: its only producer `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` in the same file is deliberately not an
instance and needs `[HasRationalPoint C]`, which has no unconditional producer either
(`hasRationalPoint_of_curve` was FALSE and is deleted, I-0491 clause 1). `HasPicSchemeEt` is the live
side; its instance `instHasPicSchemeEt` is `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1`, i.e. a projection of
the bare sorry. New work goes against `HasPicSchemeEt`/`picEt`.

THE DEAD-CONSUMER COUNT IS 74, RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-07-30 (review-ajc r5) -- and the
four the earlier censuses missed are in Jacobian.lean, the headline file. 74 declarations
bind `[HasPicScheme]` and 27 bind `[HasPicSchemeEt]`. Method unchanged from the 70 figure
(and the reason the raw-grep 90 / 75 / 88 figures were all wrong): strip block and line
comments, split each file into top-level declaration blocks, take the SIGNATURE only (up
to the first `:=` or `where`), match the bracketed binder, and count `Et` first so nothing
double-counts. The 74 sit in seven files -- Pic0AbelianVariety 34, IdentityComponent 14,
FGAPicRepresentability 9, Pic0Dimension 6, GroupSchemeHomogeneity 5, **Jacobian 4**,
HomogeneityOrbitCollapse 2 -- and the 27 in three: Pic0EtTangentSpace 12, Pic0Et 10,
FGAPicRepresentability 5.

THE FOUR IN Jacobian.lean, AND WHY THEY ARE NOT AS BAD AS THE FILE NAME SUGGESTS (checked
by reading signatures, not inferred). They are `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0`,
`finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus`, `isAlbanese_pic0`,
`isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`. Each has an `Et`-shaped sibling in the SAME file --
`smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et`, `isAlbanese_pic0Et` -- and I read both
signatures: neither carries `[HasPicScheme]` or `[HasPicSchemeEt]`, only the three
geometric binders. Those `Et` forms are the ones this board's five-obligation list names.
So the headline is stated on the live side and the `picSharp` forms are retained
development, not orphaned headline claims. The count has now been published wrong five
times running, each time omitting the file a reader opens first; the conclusion about the
74 is unaffected (see the next paragraph -- it is a theorem, not a judgement).

WHAT THE 70 MEAN -- AND THE ANSWER IS NOW A THEOREM RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT (re-measured 2026-07-30, review-ajc r4). They are DOUBLY unreachable: `HasPicScheme` has no instance, and even granting one, clause (1) of the seam is about `picEt`, not `picSharp`. So no theorem among the 70 currently speaks about any curve.

THE PART THAT WAS AN UNTESTED JUDGEMENT, and is now measured. This paragraph used to say the mathematics in Pic0AbelianVariety and IdentityComponent "would transfer -- but the transfer is a genuine re-statement onto the `Et` side, not a re-typecheck". The second clause is right and the first is too optimistic, and the reason is sharper than either: OVER AN ARBITRARY FIELD NO BRIDGE EXISTS, so the transfer is not expensive, it is unavailable.

Probed complete and axiom-clean ([propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no sorryAx, against a control that correctly reports sorryAx), as an iff:

  IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)  <-->  exists X representing picSharp C (with LocallyOfFiniteType, IsSeparated)

given the unconditional `[HasPicSchemeEt C]`. Forward: obtain the etale gate's witness and transport by `rep.ofIso (asIso (picEtComparison C)).symm` -- the SAME scheme, so both conjuncts ride along. Backward: exactly the existing `isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` (`PicEtSubcanonical.lean:310`).

WHY THAT SETTLES IT. Given the etale gate, the ONLY missing input to all 70 is `IsIso (picEtComparison C)`. The iff says that input IS picSharp representability -- which `not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso` (`:427`) plus Kleiman's pointless real conic makes FALSE over an arbitrary field. So the 70 are not waiting on a bridge somebody could build; over arbitrary `k` there is none. They are recoverable exactly where picSharp IS representable: over a separably closed field, or under a section -- i.e. as the conditional milestone, never as the headline. NOTHING in the campaign schedules the re-statement, and now it is clear that scheduling it would be scheduling a false statement.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the mechanism is the reusable part: by trying to reprice the 70 DOWNWARD and failing. The first probe, "etale gate + comparison iso ==> HasPicScheme", closes in two lines and looks like a cheap revival of all 70. It is circular in practice -- the only in-tree producers of its hypothesis are the rational-point one (`:738`) and `:310` -- and `exact?` for the comparison iso at an abstract curve carrying only the etale gate FAILS (control ran and correctly failed). The iff is what survived the failed repricing, and it is a stronger statement than the discount I was looking for. Handed to a prover lane as a hint; not landed by the reviewer.

`HasPicSchemeEt` has NOT replaced `HasPicScheme`: 27 vs 70, with the migration confined to the tangent-space chain that ajc-p2 landed this round.

AND THE HONEST QUALIFIER ON THE 27, which is the part it would be easy to sell as progress: each of the 27 is sorry-free as a DECLARATION only because it binds `[HasPicSchemeEt C]` and a bound instance is never unfolded. At a real use site `instHasPicSchemeEt` supplies it, and that instance IS `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1`. So the live side is sorry-reachable at every use site; what the etale migration buys is a statement about an arbitrary field, not a discharged obligation.

ONE OBLIGATION, TWO ROWS -- DEDUPLICATE BEFORE PROVING (review-ajc r4, 2026-07-30, and the duplication is my fault).

AJC.picrep.sepclosed-section (ajc-p3, I-1139) and AJC.picrep.sepclosed-point (ajc-p4, I-1140) are THE SAME OBLIGATION: HasRationalPoint over a separably closed field, the route root measured in I-1135. Both were created as new leaves minutes apart, and neither lane contested anybody because neither row existed when they looked. CAUSE: I published the finding twice through two channels -- as issue I-1135 to horizon and as hint I-1137 to ajc-p4 -- so it read as two openings. Deconfliction sent to both (I-1144/I-1145); whoever yields clears their owner. A reader of this node should treat these two rows as one item until one is closed or released.

WHAT I VERIFIED FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT (I-1146/I-1147): the work is a TRANSCRIPTION, not a proof. AJCR's exists_rationalPoint_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one (Curve/SeparablyClosedPoints.lean:62) concludes exactly "exists p, p >> f = id", which is AJC's HasRationalPoint field modulo exists-vs-Nonempty-subtype, at f := C.hom and X := C.left. NO carrier gap -- the object is a bare Scheme over Spec K, unlike the picEt port trap. Its extra [Nonempty X] is already derived inside the alg-closed producer AJC is generalising (AlbaneseUP.lean:293, IrreducibleSpace C.left). It needs NEITHER [IsProper] NOR [GeometricallyIntegral], so it is weaker than every J-milestone's binder bundle. Dependencies: SeparablyClosedFibre.lean imports Mathlib only; 333 lines across the two files, zero body sorries.

ORGANISATION VERDICT, re-measured 2026-07-29 (review-ajc, third pass) -- ONE item costs a lane and it is NOT the one I first named.

FIGURES AT HEAD, and note they have been cited wrongly in BOTH directions this round; re-measure before quoting. 305 modules (the brief said 172, an earlier pass said 292 then 299). 104 with a bare `import Mathlib` (brief: 66). 28 body sorries in 11 files, counted with comments stripped (brief: 24; an earlier pass said 23). QuotScheme.lean is 6265 lines, still the largest module.

THE SORRY LEDGER, 28 in 11 files: AlbaneseUP 6, Jacobian 4, Pic0AbelianVariety 3, CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional 3, SerreFiniteness 2, QuotFunctorDef 2, Pic0Et 2, IdentityComponent 2, EtaleFieldCover 2 (new this round, ajc-p1's G3 cover file), QuotRepresentability 1, FGAPicRepresentability 1 -- the last being the seam at :489, the one the whole tower projects.

WHAT COSTS NOTHING, so no lane should file it: the bare `import Mathlib` is uniform house style here, not drift; converting 104 modules is a large mechanical change with no measured payoff and would collide with the live lanes. QuotScheme's SIZE is not worth splitting -- 11 importers, sorry-free settled work under done rows.

AND I WITHDREW MY OWN 'ONE REFACTOR WORTH A LANE'S TIME' (I-0968, corrected there). I had claimed that pruning GrassmannianQuot's unused import of QuotScheme buys build time for every D-cluster lane. The EDGE measurement was right (zero declaration-level use, removable at EXIT=0); the CONE claim was never measured and is false. Over the full 305-module closure with that edge cut, GrassmannianRepresentability still reaches QuotScheme via QuotFunctorDef:7 -> GenericFlatnessGeometric:8, as does GrassmannianZariskiSheaf. 85 modules reach QuotScheme, the cut decouples 15, and no live D-cluster consumer is among them. Downgraded to hygiene: it is worth one line to whoever already has the file open, because a live-route module importing the REJECTED route's engine misleads a reader about the rejection being incomplete -- but it is not a build win and not a lane.
